reason: Accepted 30 Sep 2026: the customer's subject payload is lighter than production's average, and that is the shape being tested. Tanuh's IndividualProfile form mapping carries 2 generatable elements against production's median of 7; `make survey_bundle` reports this before any data is generated. No row count changes it, so the day-180 dataset fails this identically.
Accepted 30 Sep 2026, same cause. With 2 elements the p50 and p95 are necessarily equal, so the spread check cannot pass while the median fails for the same reason. Production's p95 is 29.

Accepted 30 Sep 2026, same cause: 119 bytes against production's 742. What it costs is recorded in the plan's parity record -- subject pull payloads and the GIN index on `individual` are both lighter than production, so subject-sync cost comes out optimistic. A green run says this shape holds at this volume.

Accepted 30 Sep 2026: the index SET matches production exactly -- 15 on encounter, 16 on individual, 17 on program_enrolment, 18 on program_encounter, confirmed by name after db-bootstrap added the sync_N family -- and an EXPLAIN of a catchment-scoped pull uses encounter_sync_1_index on all four columns in 18ms. The residual 0.33x is fill factor and bloat, not absence: these were built by CREATE INDEX over loaded data so they pack near 90% with no dead entries, while production's grew through years of inserts where page splits settle around 70% and dead entries persist until a REINDEX these tables rarely get. Recorded in the parity record as understating index scan and maintenance cost.
